key_insight: Maximal convective heat transport is governed by marginal energy stability, not by turbulence intensity, and can occur with near-optimal mean temperature profiles.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a route to high wall heat flux in thermal systems without sustaining turbulence, potentially enabling more efficient heat-transfer designs.
method: Used marginal energy-stability theory to identify near-optimal mean temperature profiles.
Compared predicted fluxes with optimal transport states and rigorous upper bounds.
Constructed equivalent internally forced conductive states and tested them in DNS.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports asymptotic scaling Nu ~ 0.0245 Ra^{1/2} and DNS showing a turbulent flow relaxes to a motionless high-flux state.
watch_item: The conductive high-flux state relies on prescribed internal thermal forcing, so practical implementation may be difficult in real devices.
paper_title: Optimal heat transport at the edge of energy stability
